newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCIETE GENERALE TAKES STAKE IN CZECH MND.
newsitem.headline: SOCIETE GENERALE TAKES STAKE IN CZECH MND.

text.p: France's Societe Generale has acquired a 39.75 percent stake in the Czech oil surveyor Moravske Naftove Doly , according to a filing with the Czech Central Securities Registry (SCP) on Thursday.

A Societe Generale reprsentative in Prague, Jaroslav Nedbal, told Reuters after the filing that the French bank bought a 37 percent stake in a block trade with Daventree Ltd., the investment group made up of Harvard Industrial Holding and Stratton Investments.
"We bought 37 percent in a block trade with Daventree," Nedbal said. He declined to add details, or comment on whether or not Societe Generale intended to sell the stake to a third party.
It is not yet clear why there was a discrepency between the amount of shares which Societe Generale confirmed buying and the level of the stake filed with the SCP.
According to SCP filings in early December, Daventree held 21.68 percent of MFD, which is based in the southeastern part of the Czech Republic.
A spokesman for Daventree, Marek Stransky, declined immediate comment.

Other major MND shareholders, according to the most recent SCP filing, include the Czech National Property Fund, with 31.46 percent, and the investment fund managed by a unit of Komercni Banka a.s., IPF KB , with 15.23 percent.
